changes: Route sale and buyback through the existing per-account character-save journal. Check persistence availability and reconcile a prior pending save before allowing another vendor mutation.
Journal and confirm the complete Gold/bag/buyback post-image before normal replies. An unknown database result reports pending, retains recovery state and never compensates or grants another effect.
A local journal-write failure pins the latest live character using the existing save recovery mechanism. Replayed unavailable item requests do not settle twice and return both current custody views.
Keep IO outside world/actor locks, refresh owned reply snapshots after IO, and preserve ordinary prices, gear metadata, capacity and admission limits.

Fence vendor use during the still RAM-only direct trade. This avoids introducing a new durable save of a bag missing that escrow; the fence is not a replacement for the separate full two-account recovery work.

checks.focusedRace: The initial expanded vendor checks passed with Go1.27.1 race detection, package3.585s. Existing vendor reply/reward tests also pass with the new real filesystem journal fixture.
checks.finalRelatedRace: Go1.27.1 go test -race . -run '^(TestVendor|TestCharacterPersistence|TestCosmeticVendorHandler|TestCosmeticVendorPending)' -count=1 -timeout=45s passed, package4.504s. The changed call site, journal recovery and neighboring existing cosmetic persistence are covered; no broad unchanged soak was repeated.
checks.saveBarrier: The injected committer rejects any vendor reply queued before commit. Ordinary sale and buyback confirm complete saves before both custody replies; repeated requests neither settle nor save another vendor effect.
checks.reopen: For both sale and buyback, database rejection and committed-but-lost replies are exercised. Every live copy is dropped and the actual BSON journal is reopened. The existing atomic-receipt contract is modeled by the injected committer; replay settles once and preserves a later independent durable Gold credit after a lost reply.
checks.outage: Repeated failed preflight denies an inverse vendor action without another Gold/item effect. A renamed journal directory produces a real local write failure, prevents database IO, retains the latest disconnected entity, and permits exactly-once recovery/resynchronization after reopening it.
checks.unavailable: Missing persistence and an active RAM direct trade each reject vendor use before any wallet/item mutation or save.
checks.fixtureCorrections: Used the actual ClearEntityDisconnected reconnect API after an initial nonexistent helper failed compilation. A saved empty bag is correctly asserted as zero items because existing persistence omits empty slots; it is not asserted as the live bag's blank slot. No production persistence format or protection was weakened.

limits: Injected committer failures and actual local-journal reopening, not a newly assembled game binary, actual sockets, new Mongo execution, browser acceptance or production-data mutation. The unchanged CommitCharacterSave API supplies the atomic single-save receipt; live and exact-source integration gates remain for the complete milestone.

No change to current direct-trade offer or settlement persistence. Its shared frozen decision, two durable participant receipts, cancellation/full-bag recovery, startup/login and rollback compatibility remain required before1.73 release.
Forge, drops, quest/raid/event rewards and the remainder of the valuable-operation ledger remain separate work. No complete1.73, whole-economy exactly-once or capacity claim.
